data.translation: Es war einmal ein Fürst, der hatte drei Söhne. Er riet denselben zu heiraten, aber sie entgegneten: »Wir wollen nicht heiraten«. »Warum nicht?« fragte er. »Wenn wir nicht drei Schwestern heimführen können, wollen wir nicht heiraten, sonst geht unsre Familie ganz auseinander«.

data.translation: My father's eyes were full of tears. He says, "My son, if God had given you a boy, if you had a little child, I would not marry. But now you know!" I say, "Father, hold the matter back until the forty days for the deceased woman are completed; leave it to God and me. I will go and bring you a woman myself, and you will need nothing." He said, "My son, you know!"

rationale: Thin I Infectum-wa cell; first-person counterfactual under negation, preserving guwar-. No edition translation is available.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Jan 1.47/2098)

data.turoyo: Ǧan: ʕAmmo Išoʕ əno ste maṭino, i naqqa səryoye mə Məḏyaḏ ya ste mə lə ḥḏor d Məḏyaḏ d gəwriwo ʕam noše mi Qaməšlo ya lə ḥḏore di Qaməšlo. Ġalabe naqqat hat d əmmina, hat ʕəbratwo baš šuġlonaṯṯe, məfqatwolən nəfusat. Aydarbo məfqatwolən nəfusat?
data.translation: Jan: Uncle Isho, I too have reached that time, the time when Syriacs from Midyat, or also from around Midyat, used to marry people from Qamishli or around Qamishli. Very often you, let us say, you used to enter into these affairs; you used to obtain identity papers for them. How did you obtain identity papers for them?

rationale: Thin I Infectum-wa cell; repeated cross-border marriages with explicit ʕam spouse expression. No edition translation is available.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infinitiv (Jan 1.47/2104)

data.turoyo: <...> Sayminawola, manṭenawo əšme dayo, maḥtinawola ʕal əšma w məfqinawola daskara d nəfus w sayminawo u gəworaṯṯe. <...>
data.translation: Uncle Isho: She cannot be registered. It is not possible. Her mother and father had to be Turkish citizens, for her to be one. Then we used to be compelled to bring a woman who had... who had died and remained in the register without a death entry, and who had been unmarried. We used to do it for her; we used to bring that woman's name, put her under her name, obtain a civil-register card for her, and perform their marriage. And we used to get her through. Then it was another name. Under her own name too it was not possible.

rationale: Thin I Infinitiv cell; possessed event nominal as object of sayminawo in marriage registration, distinct from round-1 dlo gworo. No edition translation is available.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Jan 2.2/107)

data.turoyo: <...> W bu kṯowo ste, bu gəworo flan, d luwewo raḥuqo, d luwewo bavəkat raḥuqe, baynoṯayye lə gəwriwo. əmmiwo: "Mamnuʕ! I ʕito lo kobo rəxṣa." <...>
data.translation: Chorepiscopus Brahim: They brought this out in the church so that the people would become kin with one another, so that they would love one another. So that they would become one family, so that they would become kin with one another. And among us we also used to count a ritual kinsman as a brother. And in writing too, in marriage and such, if he were a distant relative, if he had distant parents, they would not marry one another. They used to say, 'Forbidden! The church does not give permission.' So that the people, those distant from one another, would become kin with one another, like that; that is why it is like this.

rationale: Thin I Infectum-wa cell; negated customary intermarriage with reciprocal baynoṯayye. No edition translation is available.

summary: I.1 already includes marriage and consummation. The latter is explicit in PrS 11/22 and 35/112, so no new sense is needed. Partner ʕam- occurs in JTM 3.4/13,19; finite feminine gawiro differs from state gawərto.
III.1 expresses arranging another person's marriage with zero/l- human patients and l- spouse expressions. The existing 29/315 example instead has wife subject and b-spouse, hence new III.2.
Preterit Magwallilux in 78/143,146 is a marriage declaration performed by saying it; the repeated declaration is not quoted twice.

Old prs page/line references and supplied PrS text/verse references are not treated as contradictory automatically. Already quoted passages are not duplicated, including the Imperativ formula and 26/1.
gawri in 57/218 and məgwər in JTM 4.5/4 remain morphologically uncertain. No box is added on their basis.

Jan Beṯ-Şawoce provides no edition translation. English in the input is machine translation and is not quoted as an edition translation. Added examples therefore have an empty translation field; meanings are assessed from the Turoyo.

I qaṭəl feminine gawiro/gawirono contrasts with Part act. gawərto; plural gawire appears with past copulas and includes married daughters as well as sons. Event completion and resulting state must be separated by morphology and context.
III.1 in Jan still means arranging another person's marriage; these data neither duplicate nor independently establish round 1's III.2 with b-spouse.

gəworo in administrative assistance or sayminawo u gəworaṯṯe names marriage as an event, without proving that the verb means certify or obtain papers. The transparent light-verb expression is noted rather than given another numbered sense.
